"Ticket" for the andesim repo means a **Gitea issue** on the origin remote
`https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim`. There is no in-repo ticket

2026-09-06.

The login is already configured under the name `andes` (created from the
`~/.git-credentials` password; tea minted its own access token on the server).

tea issues create --login andes --repo nick/hybrid_sim \
  --title "..." --description "$BODY"
tea issues list --login andes --repo nick/hybrid_sim

The repo has **no labels and no milestones defined**, so don't pass
`--labels`/`--milestone` until some are created. Bodies render GitHub-flavored
markdown (tables work).

are the natural ticket titles — see [[andesim-linux-runtime-roadmap]].

# #20 release: on Linux, andesim must run inside the container              
  transparently, with shared memory sized to the run (open)                   
                                                                              
  @nick created 2026-09-08 10:07                                              
                                                                              
  ## Problem                                                                  
                                                                              
  AndeSim v0.1.0 is delivered as a container image that each user builds      
  themselves. That image holds everything a run needs: the driver, QEMU, the  
  cycle-accurate engine, and a RISC-V toolchain. The user should never have to
  know a container is involved — they type an AndeSim command and get a cycle 
  number.                                                                     
                                                                              
  Today only macOS gets that. On macOS the AndeSim entry point re-executes the
  command inside a container. On Linux it runs a locally built binary         
  directly, so a Linux user of the image would have to compose container      
  invocations by hand.                                                        
                                                                              
  There is also a failure waiting for the first Linux user who runs hybrid    
  mode inside a container. A hybrid run needs a shared memory region under    
  /dev/shm that both the functional leg and the cycle-accurate leg map. A     
  container gets 64 MB of /dev/shm by default. The standard tests already need
  128 MB, and Linux-runtime workloads need several gigabytes. Without         
  handling, the first hybrid run a user tries fails.                          
                                                                              
  ## Required Behavior                                                        
                                                                              
  On Linux, when an AndeSim image is available, running the AndeSim entry     
  point on the host must execute the requested command inside that image, and

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# andesim: repo-root entry for the C++ driver (build/andesim).

if [ "${ANDESIM_OS:-$(uname -s)}" = "Darwin" ]; then
  exec bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_in_container.sh" "$@"
fi

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >&2
exec "$BIN" "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run andesim inside the AndeSim image (see Containerfile, built by
# scripts/build_image.sh) -- the macOS path: macOS is run-only, because both
# hybrid legs must share one Linux kernel.
#
# Three rules make a containerised run behave like a local one:
#   1. The shared mmap stays VM-local: the container's /dev/shm (--shm-size)
#      is tier 1, and the host's HSIM_MMAP_DIR is never forwarded -- a host
#      path would be a virtiofs mount, where MAP_SHARED is not coherent.
#   2. The caller's cwd is bind-mounted at the SAME path, so relative ELF
#      arguments and output files behave as if the run were local (plain
#      file IO is fine across the boundary; only the mmap is not).
#   3. The RISC-V toolchain is bind-mounted read-only at the canonical
#      in-image path. The image deliberately does not carry a toolchain; it
#      is the user's, and the image's own config.env already names this path.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

# The canonical in-image toolchain mount point, shared with the image build.
IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/riscv-toolchain

ENGINE="${ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE:-}"
if [ -z "$ENGINE" ]; then
  if command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then ENGINE=podman
  elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then ENGINE=docker
  else
    echo "andesim: a macOS run executes inside a Linux VM and needs podman (or docker)" >&2
    echo "           install podman and run: podman machine init && podman machine start" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
fi

# VERSION is the single source of truth for the tag scripts/build_image.sh
# applies, so a version bump cannot desync the build from the run.
IMAGE="${ANDESIM_IMAGE:-andesim:$(cat "$ROOT/VERSION" 2>/dev/null || echo latest)}"
SHM_SIZE="${ANDESIM_SHM_SIZE:-3g}"   # tier 1 ceiling inside the VM

# The image declares its own ENTRYPOINT, so the user's arguments go straight
# to it. Passing the entry path as an argument as well made the driver see its
# own path as an operand ("unexpected argument 'run'"). ANDESIM_IMAGE_ENTRY
# stays available as an override, applied the only way that works.
ENTRY_ARGS=()
if [ -n "${ANDESIM_IMAGE_ENTRY:-}" ]; then
  ENTRY_ARGS=(--entrypoint "$ANDESIM_IMAGE_ENTRY")
fi

# The toolchain the caller has: the exported value, else config.env's.
TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}"
if [ -z "$TOOLCHAIN" ] && [ -f "$ROOT/config.env" ]; then
  TOOLCHAIN=$(sed -n 's/^HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=//p' "$ROOT/config.env" | tr -d '"' | head -1)
fi
TOOLCHAIN_ARGS=()
if [ -n "$TOOLCHAIN" ] && [ -d "$TOOLCHAIN" ]; then
  TOOLCHAIN_ARGS=(-v "$TOOLCHAIN:$IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN:ro")
fi

TTY_ARGS=()
if [ -t 0 ] && [ -t 1 ]; then TTY_ARGS=(-it); fi

exec "$ENGINE" run --rm "${TTY_ARGS[@]}" \
  --shm-size "$SHM_SIZE" \
  -v "$PWD:$PWD" \
  "${TOOLCHAIN_ARGS[@]}" \
  -w "$PWD" \
  "${ENTRY_ARGS[@]}" \
  "$IMAGE" "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F4 contract: on macOS the wrapper re-execs `andesim` inside the prebuilt
# Linux runtime image (both legs must share one Linux kernel). Verified on
# Linux with a stub container engine (ANDESIM_OS=Darwin forces the branch):
#
#   - the container gets --shm-size (the mmap's tier 1 lives in the VM)
#   - the caller's cwd is bind-mounted at the same path (ELF inputs/outputs)
#   - HSIM_MMAP_DIR is never forwarded (a host path would cross the VM
#     boundary, where MAP_SHARED is not coherent)
#   - the image's own baked driver is the entry; user args forward verbatim
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

TMP=$(mktemp -d -t andes-macos.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# Stub engine: records its argv and env, runs nothing.
cat > "$TMP/stub-engine" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
printf '%s\n' "$@" > "$STUB_OUT"
env > "$STUB_ENV"
exit 0
EOF
chmod +x "$TMP/stub-engine"

run_wrapped() {
  (cd "$TMP" && \
   STUB_OUT="$TMP/argv" STUB_ENV="$TMP/env" \
   ANDESIM_OS=Darwin \
   ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE="$TMP/stub-engine" \
   HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/Users/u/scratch \
   "$ROOT/andesim" "$@" </dev/null)
}

run_wrapped run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --mem-size 256M my.elf \
  || fail "Darwin wrapper exited non-zero"
[ -f "$TMP/argv" ] || fail "stub engine was never invoked"
ARGV=$(cat "$TMP/argv")

has() { printf '%s\n' "$ARGV" | grep -qx -- "$1"; }

has "run"                 || fail "engine argv missing 'run':"$'\n'"$ARGV"
has "--shm-size"          || fail "missing --shm-size (VM-local mmap tier 1):"$'\n'"$ARGV"
has "$TMP:$TMP"           || fail "cwd not bind-mounted at the same path:"$'\n'"$ARGV"
has "-w"                  || fail "missing workdir:"$'\n'"$ARGV"
has "my.elf"              || fail "user args not forwarded:"$'\n'"$ARGV"
has "--mem-size"          || fail "user flags not forwarded:"$'\n'"$ARGV"
printf '%s\n' "$ARGV" | grep -qx "andesim:$(cat "$ROOT/VERSION")" \
  || fail "default image name (andesim:<VERSION>) absent:"$'\n'"$ARGV"
printf '%s\n' "$ARGV" | grep -q "HSIM_MMAP_DIR" \
  && fail "HSIM_MMAP_DIR must not cross into the VM:"$'\n'"$ARGV"
printf '%s\n' "$ARGV" | grep -qx -- "-it" \
  && fail "no TTY here, so -it must be absent:"$'\n'"$ARGV"

# ANDESIM_IMAGE overrides the image.
(cd "$TMP" && \
 STUB_OUT="$TMP/argv2" STUB_ENV="$TMP/env2" \
 ANDESIM_OS=Darwin \
 ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE="$TMP/stub-engine" \
 ANDESIM_IMAGE=registry.example/andes:v2 \
 "$ROOT/andesim" run --mode fast my.elf </dev/null) \
  || fail "wrapper with ANDESIM_IMAGE exited non-zero"
grep -qx "registry.example/andes:v2" "$TMP/argv2" \
  || fail "ANDESIM_IMAGE not honored:"$'\n'"$(cat "$TMP/argv2")"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release-surface contract: the andesim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
# user-facing commands (run, profile, list, doctor) and never the third-party
# simulator name "verilator". The former developer commands build/test/state-diff
# have moved OUT of the binary (build -> scripts/build_all.sh, test ->
# scripts/test_all.sh, state-diff -> the diff_states core behind `run --verify`):
# they are not listed in any help and are not dispatchable. The removed /
# never-shipped commands (cluster, archive, replay, estimate) must
# not be advertised in any help. The cycle-accurate engine is presented as "vsim" everywhere --
# proven end to end with a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator" and
# must come back out as vsim:.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

require_driver

# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }

# 1. release --help: a clear command TREE -- run/list/doctor are the major
# commands (column 0); each is followed by its indented subcommands (run's
# modes, list's targets); run carries its full option list with REQUIRED flags
# marked. No developer-commands section, no "verilator", no dev-only fixtures.
H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
has '^run '     "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'run':"$'\n'"$H"
has '^profile ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'profile':"$'\n'"$H"
has '^list '    "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'list':"$'\n'"$H"
has '^doctor '  "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'doctor':"$'\n'"$H"
for s in fast cycle hybrid; do
  has "^  $s " "$H" || fail "release --help: run missing subcommand '$s':"$'\n'"$H"
done
for t in models engines; do
  has "^  $t " "$H" || fail "release --help: list missing target '$t':"$'\n'"$H"
done
has 'REQUIRED for hybrid' "$H" || fail "release --help: --trigger not marked REQUIRED for hybrid:"$'\n'"$H"
for c in build test state-diff cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "(^|  )$c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
done
no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has 'developer command' "$H" && fail "release --help: developer commands moved to scripts/; drop the section:"$'\n'"$H"
has '^  fixtures ' "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked dev-only 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$H"
ok "release --help: run/list/doctor tree with subcommands + REQUIRED flags, no dev/removed surface"

# 2. The developer commands left the binary entirely: ANDESIM_DEV=1 --help adds
# NO commands (run/list/doctor only) -- it only reveals the dev 'fixtures'
# target. build/test/state-diff are not dispatchable.
D=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
for c in run profile list doctor; do
  has "^$c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing major command '$c':"$'\n'"$D"
done
for c in build test state-diff cluster archive replay estimate; do
  has "(^|  )$c " "$D" && fail "dev --help: leaked removed/hidden command '$c'"
done
has '^  fixtures ' "$D" || fail "dev --help: should reveal the dev 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$D"
no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
# Not dispatchable as commands: since the default-command rule (run may be
# omitted), an unknown first word parses as `run`'s own argument and fails
# run's validation -- it must NOT reach any build/test/state-diff behavior.
for c in build test state-diff; do
  expect 2 "run: --mode fast.cycle.hybrid is required" "$BIN" "$c"
done
ok "dev --help: dev 'fixtures' target revealed, no developer commands; build/test/state-diff parse as run args and fail (rc 2)"

# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:; the
# --trigger menu offers only the supported triggers (marker|pc).
RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"
no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
has ' --mem-size' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --mem-size:"$'\n'"$RH"
has ' --mmap-size' "$RH" && fail "run --help: retired --mmap-size alias should stay hidden:"$'\n'"$RH"
# Interactive-debug + oracle knobs are user-facing: documented in the release help.
has '^  --verify '   "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --verify:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --print-memmap ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --print-memmap:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb '      "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --gdb-port ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb-port:"$'\n'"$RH"
# The ROI pipeline-trace knobs are user-facing: --kanata, with --objdump
# nested under it (it requires --kanata, like the pc pair under --trigger).
has '^  --kanata '    "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --kanata:"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^    --objdump ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --objdump nested under --kanata:"$'\n'"$RH"
# run --help is sliced from the same tree: it shows the mode subcommands and
# marks the required flags (so a user sees --trigger is mandatory for hybrid).
has '^  fast '   "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing mode subcommand 'fast':"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  hybrid ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing mode subcommand 'hybrid':"$'\n'"$RH"
has '^  --trigger ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --trigger:"$'\n'"$RH"
has 'REQUIRED for hybrid' "$RH" || fail "run --help: --trigger not marked REQUIRED for hybrid:"$'\n'"$RH"
ok "run --help: vsim: example, modes + REQUIRED markers, no verilator, --mem-size/--verify/--gdb documented"

# 4. list models: composition cells read vsim (never verilator), and NOTES show
# user-facing model traits only -- no implementation detail.
LM=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1)
has 'vsim' "$LM" || fail "list models: missing vsim"
no_word "$LM" || fail "list models: leaked 'verilator'"
for d in 'transparent passthrough' 'pure from reset'; do
  has "$d" "$LM" && fail "list models: leaked implementation detail '$d':"$'\n'"$LM"
done
ok "list models: vsim, no verilator, no implementation detail"

# 5. list engines end to end: a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator"
# must surface as vsim: (the single normalization point), proving --engine /
# errors / list all speak the product name with no real sim_* needed.
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat >"$TMP/sim_fake" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"verilator:fakecfg","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
EOF
chmod +x "$TMP/sim_fake"
LE=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" list engines 2>&1)
has 'vsim:fakecfg' "$LE" || fail "list engines: fake not renamed to vsim:fakecfg:"$'\n'"$LE"
no_word "$LE" || fail "list engines: leaked 'verilator':"$'\n'"$LE"
# Triggers are a hybrid-MODEL option, not an engine attribute: `list engines`
# carries no TRIGGERS column.
has 'TRIGGERS' "$LE" && fail "list engines: TRIGGERS is a hybrid-model option, not an engine column:"$'\n'"$LE"
ok "list engines: a verilator-self-describing engine is shown as vsim:, no TRIGGERS column"

# 6. `list fixtures` is a developer target (internal test ELFs, not user
# workloads): release list --help hides the target line; ANDESIM_DEV reveals
# it. (Checked as the '^  fixtures ' target line, not the bare word -- doctor's
# brief legitimately mentions checking fixtures are present.)
LH=$("$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
has '^  fixtures ' "$LH" && fail "release list --help: leaked 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$LH"
has '^  models '   "$LH" || fail "release list --help: missing 'models' target:"$'\n'"$LH"
expect 2 "unknown target 'fixtures'" "$BIN" list fixtures
DLH=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
has '^  fixtures ' "$DLH" || fail "dev list --help: missing 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$DLH"
ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list fixtures >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "dev: list fixtures should succeed"
ok "list: fixtures is dev-only (release hides it; ANDESIM_DEV reveals it)"

# 7. The removed `build` command must not survive in user-facing hints: a
# missing artifact in `doctor` now points at scripts/build_all.sh.
#
# Driven through the plugin row, which scripts/build_all.sh genuinely builds.
# It used to be driven through the vsim row and a VSIM_BIN override, but that
# variable was read nowhere except that row: it could report vsim missing
# while the driver ran a discovered engine perfectly well. The row now follows
# engine discovery, and an engine is built in the external vsim checkout,
# which build_all.sh does not do.
DOC=$(VSIM_PLUGIN=/no/such/plugin "$BIN" doctor 2>&1 || true)
printf '%s\n' "$DOC" | grep -q 'andesim build' && fail "doctor hint still names the removed 'andesim build':"$'\n'"$DOC"
printf '%s\n' "$DOC" | grep -q 'scripts/build_all.sh' || fail "doctor hint should point at scripts/build_all.sh:"$'\n'"$DOC"
ok "doctor missing-artifact hint points at scripts/build_all.sh, not the removed command"

ok "release surface (hide verilator + release/dev command split)"

# Issue #24 contract, verified against a built image: what the image actually
# contains. tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_image_build.sh covers the build
# plan; this covers the product of that plan.
#
# Skips when the image has not been built on this machine -- building it takes
# hours (Verilating the RTL), so it cannot be a precondition of the standard
# suite. Build it with scripts/build_image.sh, then this runs for real.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

ENGINE=ax46mpv_fpga_l3
IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/riscv-toolchain
IMAGE="${ANDESIM_IMAGE:-andesim:$(cat "$ROOT/VERSION")}"

RUNTIME="${ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE:-}"
if [ -z "$RUNTIME" ]; then
  if command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then RUNTIME=podman
  elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then RUNTIME=docker
  else ok "no container runtime here -- skipping image contents"; exit 0
  fi
fi

if ! "$RUNTIME" image exists "$IMAGE" 2>/dev/null; then
  ok "$IMAGE not built here -- skipping image contents (scripts/build_image.sh)"
  exit 0
fi

# in_image CMD...  -- run a shell command inside the image, nothing mounted.
in_image() {
  "$RUNTIME" run --rm --entrypoint /bin/sh "$IMAGE" -c "$1" 2>&1
}

# --- the image runs AndeSim with no QEMU and no engine prepared outside ------
out=$(in_image '/opt/andesim/andesim list engines')
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qw "$ENGINE" \
  || fail "the image does not report the $ENGINE engine:"$'\n'"$out"

# Exactly one cycle-accurate engine. Every other config is deferred, and each
# one would add a Verilator run to the slowest step of the build.
engines=$(in_image 'ls "$VSIM_BIN_DIR" | grep "^sim_" | sort')
[ "$engines" = "sim_$ENGINE" ] \
  || fail "the image must hold sim_$ENGINE and nothing else, found:"$'\n'"$engines"

out=$(in_image '"$VSIM_QEMU" --version')
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qi 'qemu' \
  || fail "the image's QEMU does not run:"$'\n'"$out"

# The handoff plugin and the runtime library are AndeSim's own artifacts; the
# runtime library existing proves the mounted toolchain built it.
in_image 'test -f "$VSIM_PLUGIN"' \
  || fail "the hybrid handoff plugin is missing from the image"
in_image 'test -f /opt/andesim/build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a' \
  || fail "the runtime library is missing -- the build-time toolchain mount failed"

# --- the toolchain is the user's, mounted; the image carries neither it nor -
# --- any path from the machine that built the image -------------------------
# The mount point exists and is empty. Existing matters: a missing directory
# gave "No such file or directory" with nothing in the image to hint at what
# to mount, where an empty one shows the shape the run expects.
in_image "test -d $IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN" \
  || fail "$IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN does not exist, so a forgotten mount says only" \
          " 'No such file or directory'"
left=$(in_image "ls -A $IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN | wc -l")
[ "$left" = "0" ] \
  || fail "$IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN holds $left entries -- a toolchain was baked in"

# The entry point the image declares must be there and runnable.
in_image 'test -x /opt/andesim/andesim' \
  || fail "the image's ENTRYPOINT /opt/andesim/andesim is missing or not executable"

cfg=$(in_image 'cat /opt/andesim/config.env')
printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Eq "^HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN\$" \
  || fail "the image's config.env does not name the mount point:"$'\n'"$cfg"
printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Eq '/local/|/home/' \
  && fail "the image's config.env carries a host path:"$'\n'"$cfg"

in_image 'test -e /opt/andesim/.git' \
  && fail "the image carries the repository's git history"

ok "image contents: driver + QEMU + exactly the $ENGINE engine, no baked toolchain"

# Shared status printers + config/path resolution for test scripts.
# Sourced (not executed).
#
#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
#   cfg_val KEY            -> KEY's value from the repo-root config.env
#   vsim_bin_dir           -> external vsim build dir (env, then config.env)
#   qemu_bin               -> path to qemu-system-riscv64, same
#                             env-then-config.env resolution
#   shipped_cycle_engines  -> cycle-accurate engine names v0.1.0 ships
#   deferred_cycle_engines -> the ones it does not (later releases)
#
# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# Repo root, derived from this lib's own location (tests/lib/ -> ../..).
_LIB_ROOT=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)

# cfg_val KEY -> the value of KEY in the repo-root config.env ("" if absent).
# A lightweight read so a test runs without a prior `source ./setup.sh`.
cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$_LIB_ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }

# ENGINE RELEASE SURFACE -- one source of truth for the whole harness.
# v0.1.0 ships exactly two cycle-accurate engines, and the vsim side builds
# only these two (its config.yaml). Every other CPU config is deferred to a
# later release; with ax66_makatau went S/U-privilege handoff support --
# ax45mpv_premium is M-mode-only (NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1) while
# ax46mpv_fpga_l3 carries all three levels, so re-enabling S/U there is future
# work, not a v0.1.0 promise. test_andes_sim_engine_set.sh enforces that no
# test in the harness pins a deferred engine.
shipped_cycle_engines() { echo "ax45mpv_premium ax46mpv_fpga_l3"; }
deferred_cycle_engines() {
  echo "ax45mpv_premium_full ax45mpv_premium_max ax46mpv_advanced" \
       "ax46mpv_fpga_l3_bigcache_aw ax66_makatau d23"
}

# The external vsim build dir (the sim_* binaries), the way the driver resolves
# it: VSIM_BIN_DIR env, then config.env ("" when neither is set).
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  cfg_val VSIM_BIN_DIR
}

# The external QEMU build dir, resolved the same way: QEMU_BIN_DIR env, then
# config.env ("" when neither is set).
qemu_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$QEMU_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR
}

# qemu_bin -> full path of qemu-system-riscv64 in that dir (AndeSim supports
# 64-bit RISC-V only).
qemu_bin() { printf '%s/qemu-system-riscv64\n' "$(qemu_bin_dir)"; }

# Quiet driver self-build (the byte-identical preamble line of every driver
# contract test). Fatal on build failure.
build_driver() {
  bash "$_LIB_ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
}

# build_driver + point BIN at the driver binary. The caller keeps its own
# [ -x "$BIN" ] assertion (the failure messages vary per script).
require_driver() {
  BIN="$_LIB_ROOT/build/andesim"
  build_driver
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# build_image.sh -- the one command that builds a runnable AndeSim image.
#
#   scripts/build_image.sh --toolchain <path> [--tag NAME] [--dry-run]
#
# The user names a RISC-V toolchain once, here. Everything AndeSim itself
# builds -- AndeSim itself, QEMU, the ax46mpv_fpga_l3 cycle-accurate engine,
# the handoff plugin, the driver and the runtime library -- is cloned and built
# by the image build, so a run needs nothing prepared beforehand.
#
# All three sources are cloned by the build, and the build context is empty.
# Nothing from the host reaches the image: it cannot inherit a stale build/
# directory, a local config.env or an uncommitted edit, and it is reproducible
# from the three refs alone. The flip side is that a local change must be
# pushed before an image can carry it.
#
# The toolchain is never copied into the image. It is bind-mounted read-only at
# one canonical in-image path (IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN below), both while the image is
# built and when a container runs, so the image carries no host path.
#
# Building requires read access to the Andes RD-SW repositories on
# gitea.andestech.com: the engine's RTL comes from them. Access is checked
# before the long build starts, not hours into it.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

# The engine v0.1.0's image ships. Exactly one is built: Verilating the RTL is
# the slowest step of the whole build.
ENGINE=ax46mpv_fpga_l3
IMAGE_TOOLCHAIN=/opt/riscv-toolchain

# The three source repositories, each with its own ref: they do not share a
# branch name, and assuming two of them did cost a build. Overridable so an
# image can be built from a different line of development.
ANDESIM_REPO="${ANDESIM_ANDESIM_REPO:-https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim.git}"
QEMU_REPO="${ANDESIM_QEMU_REPO:-https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_qemu.git}"
VSIM_REPO="${ANDESIM_VSIM_REPO:-https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_vsim.git}"
ANDESIM_REF="${ANDESIM_ANDESIM_REF:-llamacpp}"
QEMU_REF="${ANDESIM_QEMU_REF:-andesim}"
VSIM_REF="${ANDESIM_VSIM_REF:-llamacpp}"

usage() {
  cat >&2 <<'USAGE'
usage: scripts/build_image.sh --toolchain <path> [--tag NAME] [--dry-run]

  --toolchain <path>  RISC-V toolchain root on this machine (must contain
                      bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc). Bind-mounted read-only,
                      never copied into the image.
  --tag NAME          image tag (default: andesim:<VERSION>)
  --andesim-ref REF   branch/tag of the AndeSim source (default: llamacpp)
  --qemu-ref REF      branch/tag of the QEMU source (default: andesim)
  --vsim-ref REF      branch/tag of the engine source (default: llamacpp)
  --dry-run           print the build plan and exit
USAGE
}

die() { echo "build_image.sh: $*" >&2; exit 2; }

TOOLCHAIN=""
TAG=""
DRY_RUN=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --toolchain) TOOLCHAIN="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --tag)       TAG="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --andesim-ref) ANDESIM_REF="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --qemu-ref)  QEMU_REF="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --vsim-ref)  VSIM_REF="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --dry-run)   DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help)   usage; exit 0 ;;
    *)           usage; die "unknown argument: $1" ;;
  esac
done

[ -n "$TOOLCHAIN" ] || { usage; die "--toolchain is required"; }

set -uo pipefail

for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    lint|unit|contract|e2e) PHASES+=("$arg") ;;
    *)
      echo "test_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      echo "usage: test_all.sh [--dry-run] [lint|unit|contract|e2e ...]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done
[ "${#PHASES[@]}" -eq 0 ] && PHASES=(lint unit contract e2e)

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

pass=0
failed=0
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()

  local name="$1"; shift
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "$name"; return; fi
  local log rc; log=$(mktemp)

}

#      arguments and output files behave as if the run were local (plain
#      file IO is fine across the boundary; only the mmap is not).
#   3. The RISC-V toolchain is bind-mounted read-only at the canonical
#      in-image path. The image deliberately does not carry a toolchain; it
#      is the user's, and the image's own config.env already names this path.

  grep -qxF -- "$3" "${STUB_IMAGES:-/dev/null}" 2>/dev/null
  exit $?

exit 0

     ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE="$TMP/stub-engine" \
     HSIM_MMAP_DIR=/host/scratch \

has "$TMP:$TMP"  || fail "cwd not bind-mounted at the same path:"$'\n'"$ARGV"
has "-w"         || fail "missing workdir:"$'\n'"$ARGV"
has "my.elf"     || fail "user args not forwarded:"$'\n'"$ARGV"

#   2. The caller's cwd is bind-mounted at the SAME path, so relative ELF
#      arguments and output files behave as if the run were local (plain
#      file IO is fine across the boundary; only the mmap is not).
#   3. The RISC-V toolchain is bind-mounted read-only at the canonical
#      in-image path. The image deliberately does not carry a toolchain; it
#      is the user's, and the image's own config.env already names this path.
#   4. A missing image is reported as a missing image. Left to the container
#      runtime it surfaces as a pull failure against a registry that was
#      never meant to hold it -- v0.1.0 publishes no image; each user builds

# matches what the driver will ask of it:

#              (kMmapSafetyMargin, driver/shm.hpp)

#              user names none (--runtime linux's 1G, driver/cmd_run.cpp)

# MiB. A hybrid run maps its guest RAM out of /dev/shm; a container's default
# 64 MB is below even the standard tests, and no fixed value serves both a
# 128M run and an 8G one, so the size follows the run.
shm_size_for() {

Issue #20. The image is what carries QEMU, the cycle-accurate engine and
the driver, so a run belongs inside it on every host -- not only on macOS.

    64 MB by default, below even the standard tests, and no fixed value
    serves both a 128M run and an 8G one. The size mirrors what the
    driver will ask of the tier: guest RAM + the V-scratch page + the
    resolver's free-space margin, rounded to whole MiB.

    failure against a registry that was never meant to hold it: v0.1.0
    publishes no image, each user builds their own.

    unchanged for development. The two in-tree callers that drive
    host-built artifacts -- the vlen1024 drain harness and the llama.cpp
    example, which names host paths and a host-built engine -- take it.

Issue #20 is done and verified against the real image.

## What changed

**`andesim`** — the entry point now runs inside the image on *every* host, not just macOS. The OS branch is gone. `ANDESIM_NO_CONTAINER=1` keeps the native path for driver development.

**`scripts/run_in_container.sh`** — two new behaviors:
- `--shm-size` is computed from the run's own `--mem-size` (guest RAM + the V‑scratch page + the driver's 256 MiB tier margin, rounded to whole MiB), instead of a fixed `3g`. Defaults to the 1G `--runtime linux` default when the user names no size.
- A missing image is probed for (`image inspect`) and reported by name with the command that builds one, instead of letting podman emit a registry pull error.

Two in-tree callers that drive host-built artifacts — `tests/hybrid/e2e_vlen1024_drain.sh` and `scripts/run_llama_hybrid.sh` — now take the native path explicitly.

## Verification in `/home/nick/work/build_andesim`

That directory has no `build/andesim` and no `config.env`, so every success proves the container path:

| QA step | Result |
|---|---|
| hybrid run, no container flags | `[andesim] 58 cycles` |
| output file in my own directory | `out/run.log`, owned by `nick`, at the path asked for |
| `/dev/shm` at 128M / 1G / 8G | 385 / 1281 / 8449 MiB — all runs completed |
| untag the image, run again | `andesim: no image named andesim:v0.1.0 … scripts/build_image.sh --toolchain <…>`, rc=2 |

Step 6 (macOS no-regression) I could not run here — but macOS and Linux now share one code path, and the contract test `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_container_run.sh` covers it with a stub engine.

Suite: 57 passed / 0 failed (lint + unit + contract), plus one e2e fixture on the host path.

Three commits on `llamacpp`, structural and behavioral kept separate. I have **not** pushed or closed the issue — say the word and I'll do both (the image build clones from the remote, so this needs pushing before an image can carry it).
